features: THE ATTACHMENT HAD NO PATH OF ITS OWN — This started from a forum report: after registering a supplier invoice, it no longer seemed possible to attach the PDF. That wasn't quite true — the PDF could still be attached, from the Edit form — but behind it was a real problem: an invoice attachment went through the same door as every other edit.

ATTACHING A DOCUMENT NO LONGER REWRITES THE ACCOUNTING — Before, saving an attachment redid the accrual and payment entries from scratch, even when the file was the only thing that changed. Now the attachment has its own path: it's uploaded and deleted from the Invoice Detail page, without touching the journal. The Edit form no longer handles files at all.

AN INVOICE CAN NOW HAVE MORE THAN ONE ATTACHMENT — Before, the last file uploaded silently deleted the previous one. Now you can attach as many documents as needed — the original PDF, the XML if it arrives via the exchange system, the bank transfer receipt — and they all stay, each downloadable on its own. With more than three attachments, the list scrolls instead of stretching the page indefinitely.

⚠️ THE DOCUMENT STAYS EVEN ON A CLOSED INVOICE, BUT CAN NO LONGER BE REMOVED — An attachment can still be added even to a paid, reversed, or already-closed-period invoice: a document is evidence, and adding one doesn't rewrite a balance sheet. Deleting it, though, is a different matter: once an invoice is no longer editable, its attachments stay downloadable but can't be deleted, so as not to alter the record of a closed accounting fact. If the wrong file was attached, the fix is to upload a corrected one alongside it, not to replace the old one.

A REAL .P7M ENVELOPE NOW ACTUALLY ATTACHES — A signed .p7m envelope, the kind that genuinely arrives from Italy's invoice exchange system, was always rejected, both on invoice creation and when attaching afterward, because of how the system recognized the file's content type. The check now looks at the file extension instead, the same way every other accepted format already works.

THE CONFIRMATION BEFORE DELETING AN ATTACHMENT IS NOW A REAL ONE — The Delete button on a document used to ask for confirmation through the browser's own native popup: on this page, that could look like nothing happened when you clicked. The confirmation is now the same dialog used everywhere else in the application.

THE LIST NOW SHOWS HOW MANY ATTACHMENTS AN INVOICE HAS — The paperclip icon always downloaded the first attachment, even when there were others, and never said how many there were. There's now an icon with the number written next to it: readable at a glance, including on a phone where there is no mouse. Opening them happens from the row's menu or from the invoice detail page.

THE INVOICE LIST'S DATE FILTER IS NOW A REAL RANGE — It used to be two identical fields that said neither which end was which nor which date they filtered — and this module has three. It's now a single picker with a two-month calendar that reads "Data documento" when empty. You can also pick just the start date and close the panel: that means "from this date onward". Picking a single date, the calendar asks whether it means "from" or "up to", so "every invoice up to 31 December" is still expressible. Each attachment also shows when it was uploaded, next to its size.

⚠️ THREE BUGS IN THE NEW FILTER, FOUND BY TESTING IT LIVE AND FIXED HERE — Picking two dates in quick succession could mean the second one never reached the filter: the button showed the full range while the list was filtered on the first date only — it declared one filter and applied another. A URL with a malformed date made the entire filter bar disappear, including "Azzera filtri" and "Nuova fattura". And "Azzera filtri" failed to clear the motivated-overspend filter.
